notes.title: Update: New Faction Released! - v0.2.2.2835
notes.content:
Generals!

The veil between life and death fades as the scourge of the Undead has emerged onto the battlefield!

Our newest Faction, The Order of the Undying, introduces 20 new Units and 7 new Actions, bringing countless new synergies to your skirmishes in combination with the three other existing Factions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/992756226a563411925d96924edc96dbf9d0e6d7.png[/img]
This update also includes a host of performance and bug-fixes, along with some quality of life improvements, with thanks in no small part to the amazing feedback received by our amazing community. 

As always, a big [b]THANK YOU[/b] to all the valued members of our awesome community for being with us on this journey. 

Until next time, keep smiling and keep on skirmishing!

Cheers,
The Tea Division

[url=https://discord.gg/gVEvW9S8mS][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/af5a9d83b930f4ed50b1f23d1087081373ae7bbe.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Update: New Faction "The Order of the Undying"
notes.content:
Generals!

A new Faction has clawed its way to the battlefield as [b]The Order of the Undying[/b] has come to Vanguard Exiles!

The cycle of life and death means nothing to the undead, who twist the laws of nature to their own ominous ends.

This update introduces a host of new content, featuring Units, Actions, and mechanics that empower players to raise the dead, summon skeletal warriors, or even enthrall enemies into joining the ranks of the damned. Combine these dark forces with the existing three Factions, and the strategic possibilities become limitless!

Where casualties are an inevitable part of war, The Order of the Undying is here to show that death is but the first rite in your enlistment, willing or otherwise.

No one is safe...not even the dead.

Check out the trailer video [url=https://youtu.be/Rf6StFUIYUM]here[/url].

[url=https://youtu.be/Rf6StFUIYUM][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/fae158280f4a5436b9995f8c65575a6b6aecbfec.png[/img]
[/url]
Dying to join you in the Skirmish on the [b]26th of May[/b].

[url=https://discord.gg/gVEvW9S8mS][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/af5a9d83b930f4ed50b1f23d1087081373ae7bbe.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Vanguard Exiles: Price Update
notes.content:
Generals!

First and foremost, the team would like to express their deepest gratitude towards our community for joining us on this incredible journey thus far. We've only begun to scratch the surface of what Vanguard Exiles has to offer, and are excited to continue making progress with such a phenomenal player base. 

With the release of our upcoming new Faction, The Order of the Undying, the cost for Vanguard Exiles will be getting a minor price bump of USD $5 (taking it to $19.99) which will take effect on the 26th May.

For those who've already purchased the Early Access build, there is no further cost, and this content will be in your ghoulish hands on release day!

Whilst this bump is not dramatic in terms of price increase, the impact the new content being released certainly will be! Having said this, there's still time for players to snatch this up before the price increase, and there's no better time to do so with the advent of a new Faction being introduced into the game!

As always, The Tea Division remains focused on our commitment to the community, driven by ensuring value whilst focusing on the continued growth of Vanguard Exiles and our players' experience.

More to come on the new Faction (very soon!) but until then, keep smiling and keep on skirmishing!

Cheers!
The Tea Division.

notes.title: Update: v0.1.1.2295
notes.content:
Fellow Generals! 

Well it didn't take long for the team to react to player feedback, so first patch hot off the press post-EA is already here! 

Details are as follows: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/086536290990161b24adc90df8e94cdf1636242e.png[/img]

[list]
[*]New emote wheel to communicate with your opponent in Multiplayer games
[i](Use [b]E[/b] to open the emote wheel and then mouse over and release on the emote to send it in game)
[/i][*]Updated team colours so you're always viewed as blue even if you're the client in Multiplayer games
[*]Clearer display of the unlock conditions for other Squad slots
[*]Fixed missing ∞ symbol in text Squad tool-tips for Unlimited Units and Actions
[*]Added tool-tips to the Spectator count so you can see who is spectating the game
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/d20dbd8675a2fc45254cfa8abf3802d0e0ac78ef.png[/img]

Now....what is the elusive tip you may ask? The team has been diligently spectating games, both on social channels and through the game's spectator mode, and were taken aback at how many players were asking for information that was right at their fingertips! 

[b]Players can use TOOL-TIPS on nearly anything in the game,[/b] simply by holding ALT (or pressing the middle mouse button) whilst hovering over your Units, an opponent's Units, over your opponents Score Panel in battle (or at the Barracks), where all the info you want and need is revealed! You can even do this  while you're spectating, and even during the Squad selection screen before you begin a game!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/e6a26ce4ae35dbf6af7880454bc7dd346754023d.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/70b80a3d40f09cd32d8e1f31573410f5a536eece.gif[/img]

Make no mistake....this will give you an added edge in battle! 

The team has been very active in Discord since the launch of Early Access, so now is as good a time as any to join our Discord and engage with the team and wider community. 

The Tea Division extends its thanks to our wonderful community, appreciative of the feedback and support we've received. This game is for you, so keep that feedback coming!  

As always, until next, keep smiling and keep on skirmishing!

notes.title: Vanguard Exiles: Progression of Art
notes.content:
The road to refining the art style and theme of Vanguard Exiles has been one of learning, iteration and excitement. As time progressed, it became evident that teams’ art skills were as crucial as their ability to adapt. Below we hear from the team, gaining insight into their thought processes, challenges, and how it led them during their design. 

[h3]Units[/h3]

Amongst many considerations we had, one was the toss-up between 2D or 3D. We ended up choosing 2D, and by doing so, catered to a faster iteration/turn around time. There was the whole process of figuring out aspects of the visual style along the way, but we sought a lot of reference points to guide us, one of which was Darkest Dungeon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/122cf6ebc56fe03b7e4ce7c9adc36dcf620961a5.png[/img]

We simplified our initial approach to Vanguard Exiles as having 2 sides: Red vs Blue. So we used similar design elements for our Units that complimented this angle using our various reference points and applied the relevant principles to our Units. One thing which made our Units stand out from other games though was that they were made with variant pieces, making them much more unique. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/cd4138e4a0aa15a5c15cecb93652755f003728f2.png[/img]

We wanted to move away from cards as a concept, but still allow players the flexibility to refer to each Unit as a “card”, or their Squad as their “deck”. However before this came into play, we experimented on creating unique borders for the various units (see above). E.g. Units that employed magic would have a specific “Mage” themed icon, Units that could attack at a distance would have an associated “Ranged” icon, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/123d2a261fe94663c8a4cfea71a70226cbd4c2ef.png[/img]

Above are examples of earlier designs for the Scout and Cavalier Units. There were a whole bunch of variant pieces for these templates, designed in a way that allowed flexibility in each units’ parts, giving us the option to swap out parts for each of these units as needed/intended. The Units have a very strong comic book style emphasis, with strong angular features that accent their movement and graphics in game. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/3cfe540e3352d65dc7578d0805586143b3d4915e.png[/img]

An enjoyable part of the process was experimenting with proportions and body shapes (indicated via some of the early concepts above). The Tank (champion) was intentionally massive comparatively to the Scout, who was designed to be a smaller, more agile unit. The Cavalier was somewhere in the middle of those, having a medium build, but still wielding a shield and mace. With the Mage, we envisioned a Unit who had formidable skills, with a less formidable frame, opting to make him slim and tall. Not all these concepts (and some of the following iterations) were utilized in the end, but they acted as a solid foundation for any redesigning as feedback was received from the designer, Richard Garfield. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/c7a9a1d2e7a9b78f41a37a4ce72997c141efef97.png[/img]

The theme for the world was one that resonated perfectly, both in design and execution. Revolving around a steampunk/fantasy world amidst a landscape heavily influenced by WWI, the team worked towards a cinematic trailer to really capture the essence of the theme, and bring cohesion to the various aspects. The result of which can be seen on the Vanguard Exiles Steam page or [url=https://www.youtube.com/@VanguardExiles]YouTube channel[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/47e392919784507056e1d3e4139aea0a6c0eb78f.png[/img]

The above Elf and Dwarf designs were quite early concepts that ended up being utilized with some minor tweaking. The exploration in designs which were initially focused around a card base feel, deviated from this when the card was utilized in game, transitioning from a “card in hand” to “Unit in play.” Despite moving away from the card theme, the initial explorations influenced by the perspective of the Units being cards did well for stylization, and really enabled the team to narrow down the aesthetic for the various creatures/Factions, to later then integrate the WWII flavor into the design. Even in the earlier design stages, the Dwarves felt on point, especially when we added the flavor of having access to things like Turrets or a Steam Tank to deploy. The Berserker Bear was a favored design too, heavily influenced from the popular Netflix series “Love, Sex and Robots.” 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/15e4e8a28798938bbba47c9069c0f7ee73b1712c.png[/img]



[h3]VFX[/h3]

Our goal for VFX was to ensure that they were easily notifiable in the zones, regardless of the angle they were viewed from. Some did well to match the specific zone they were allocated to, naming the "Boggin Temple" as an example, while others needed to be more flexible so as to suit any zone they may be placed within.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/e3450bac962e27d524b3dfd0ec3e578bb3e198f7.gif[/img]

A consistent focus throughout the process was to ensure the VFX was readable, engaging, and optimized for performance. The key element in this process was the players’ perspective, honing down on the principle where players should easily understand the effects both in battle mode and from a higher map view. There were certainly challenges with this, especially with effects that had variations. Poison spells were a good example of this, as they need to be distinct from other effects, yet similar enough across its various applications and origin, regardless of whether the effect came from a nearby unit or from a distance. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/e7492f4988b79dcea57a8a2a31427c3e97c2f4b5.gif[/img]

Another consideration was the dynamic camera movements created by the game’s Director system. With the camera in play, the VFX could be seen in various screen positions, but the goal was to ensure that players could still recognize the effects in play., whilst considering that  VFX could trigger from various sources such as spells, abilities, zone effects, and nearby units. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/3d9f09aba0f6349c397cf98ed90e04cbf2f283de.gif[/img]

Throughout the development of Vanguard Exiles, a number of aspects have undergone changes to ensure VFX alignment with these aspects appeared natural and/or appropriate. These aspects included things such as camera angles, Unit movement, Unit positioning during combat, and the tweaking of timing across these various aspects. Another consideration we had was ensuring the players weren’t overwhelmed by multiple visual effects that could occur simultaneously, so observing VFX during different playthroughs at various angles and distances became paramount for the team to make the necessary adjustments. Despite the VFX still being in earlier iterations, they have laid a solid foundation for any future iterations to be made, bringing added emphasis to the combat and immersion in each game.


[h3]Zones[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/ae70be0a87233556832a6d6f28418694311b2098.png[/img]

The zones went through a number of concepts and styles before we settled on the final design,  ranging from classic fantasy dungeons, sky-punk castles, to a map opening sequence influenced by the opening sequence in Game of Thrones. Ultimately we liked the idea of it being a battlefield that's gradually explored and expanded, but one that can also degrade as the war wages on. In doing this, the games’ battlefield is open to the likely potential to appear very different from how it did at the start, giving the player a greater sense of immersion in an evolving (or devolving) landscape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/b2eeaaa11165825411ff8828725110873df48357.png[/img]

Initially we looked at hexagon-shaped tiles, which work well for exploration and strategy games, but we wanted to change and expand from this, and in doing so came the inclusion of corridors. Strategically, corridors easily facilitated newer strategies, like creating choke-points, and changed the dynamic of the map, going from a big open field where Units can go in any direction, to an evolving map with areas that changed the landscape of the battlefield as each round progressed. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/516d6b7260853b7e55861dca4fa99d06cc641298.gif[/img] 

The zones have a capture ring around them - an important feature that shows the progression as the zones are being captured. One of the design decisions was to steer away from making the zones perfect hexagons, and create a curved indent at the corners. This made it much easier for the player to see how the zones connect and how units would traverse them, passing through where they directly connected, rather than where three hexagon corners would connect. Once in place, this in turn affected the design of the capture ring, leading to a mechanic that felt well suited to how the game plays.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/d8e1b3be94d94e0c5699e0b7cc567ac1a5162435.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/5d8987afccb3675ec012f73f0e0bddd6abbc0fb3.png[/img]

Currently there are three biomes for the zones:  

[list]
[*]Trench - bunkers and holes carved into the ground for Units to hide and hope for the best
[*]Ruins - a once beautiful city devoted to the study of sorcery, now lying in rubble and ruin
[*]Deep Ruins - due to the cataclysmic upheaval of war, these ruins became exposed to the open sky after centuries underground, where to this day, the creation of these ancient tunnels is still a mystery at to who dug them and why  
[/list]

With every design challenge presented, the excitement of iteration and solution has driven the team to not only overcome the obstacles before them, but exceed expectations with their learnings, moving forward with a fresher perspective and ever-ready for the next challenge. The evolution of Vanguard Exiles from the (now) available demo on Steam to the coming build planned for Early Access will highlight the significant leap the team has made, who are nothing short of eager to showcase it to Generals everywhere.

notes.title: Vanguard Exiles: The Journey Begins
notes.content:
The journey of Vanguard Exiles has already been an exciting one. And once we began, The Tea Division discovered we had a goal: to share our excitement with our players by giving you insight into where we started and, perhaps more importantly, where we’re headed! With a focus on providing updates on development, progress, and upcoming features, The Tea Division is committed to ensuring you, our players, are a key part of our journey as we drive toward Early Access.

It only takes one game of Vanguard Exiles to see just how deep it can be. With an abundance of strategy and as-yet undiscovered armies, styles, and tactics, it’s a difficult task for us to even decide where to begin.

Or so we thought—until we realized there was nowhere better to start than with words of the man who actually designed the game! And so, here is some insight from the legendary game designer himself, Richard Garfield, as he talks about the beginning of Vanguard Exiles!

[quote=Richard Garfield][b]The Map
[/b]
The very first concept that led to Vanguard Exiles was “an autobattler with a meaningful map.” 

I was interested in a game in which players were not only building their best army over time but also one in which deployment was an interesting and accessible part of the game. In many autobattlers, the configuration is important, but all the battling is taking place in the same room, where often the configuration is something only advanced players can really appreciate. 

I envisaged a game in which each player would choose where their various warriors started—the rooms would be fought over somewhat independently and would often give players something different as a reward for claiming that individual room. 

Below, you can see the very first sketch I made to communicate the idea, a simple five-room layout with different effects, victory points, and interesting topography:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/b71321e2b2d845385ea8ff4e5d91efe9a18f9246.png[/img]
I honestly can’t remember what the red line was meant to indicate—I think it might have been a connection just for use by archers—but there were some drafts where we were considering having pathways that only small creatures could pass through as well.

This concept excited everyone, and we talked about the many ways to do the map. The map could look like 
[list]
[*] a dungeon on a rectangular grid, or
[*] a world map with hexagons, or
[*] something that was more free form 
[/list]
Turns out, there are a lot of things you can do with a map! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/07c6afd86531dcddb629419e984a0447d307e340.jpg[/img]
In very early versions, this was entirely on a hex map, with each hex having access to neighboring hexes. This was nice—it had a good look, and the relationship between the rooms was easy to see. This also made it easy to see how we could vary the map over time by adding rooms to the edges. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/3edc412cd20ebff9df40e7bf2bffff5a269f3bc0.png[/img]
This was also really nice because I didn't want the same map each time. However, entirely changing the map would make things too crazy, with no sense of achieving mastery from round to round and no way of ever getting to know a particular layout. Eventually, we developed a system by which we could both add and remove rooms from the layout in such a way that the scale of the dungeon could grow with your army. We also added corridors, which made the layout of the map more interesting by limiting connectivity and made some rooms farther apart than they otherwise would be. 

By introducing higher-value rooms and wackier room effects over time, we got a nice feel for how the game would change during the course of play. It would begin simple with lower stakes and would generally grow in complexity and stakes along the way. This provided the tools to allow players to have a meaningful early game experience but not feel overwhelmed or so far behind they couldn’t catch up.

[b]Flavor
[/b]
We talked about lots of possible flavors and eventually settled on a sort of fantasy World War I setting. The relationship between trenches and dungeons felt like a fun one to explore—and The Tea Division developed some concept art that really made it feel fresh but understandable.
 
I was particularly taken with the idea of making elves scientific rather than “natural,” being at one with the forest and all of that. We did keep them “elfy” by having ranged fighters and by them being fast (and dodging at inopportune times), but I also made sure they had damage over time; e.g., from radiation effects. I loved the idea of the elves walking around bathed in scary-looking green “science” light.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/b80594b47fbf4aa42b80dca17f4841ebc41f3b3e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/3178d7dba343a88399f28700d68304ea0a8320bc.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/c86b55b559120c845504203485b7e763c80f4f30.png[/img]

The idea of trenches interspersed with proper dungeon environments felt especially good. We decided it would be nice to always begin in the trenches but that the tile set we drew from would change from game to game and perhaps season to season. The sewers. Abandoned labs. Old ruins. Ice caverns. Forgotten temples. All these wild environments could start with something familiar and be uncovered over the course of the game. And, of course, it wouldn’t be just a different wallpaper. You would expect different things from the lava tubes than you would expect from the necropolis.

The world easily supported a wide variety of factions, ones that would be characterized by different strengths, weaknesses, and allies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/eaaaadd681ab4ec48c1b1bf26aa8b3253a07e74a.jpg[/img]

[b]Armies and Squads
[/b]
A player’s deck (or Squad) is the set of creatures and actions that they have access to. Their starting hand (or Vanguard) are the ones they have at a particular point in a game.

I wanted to see each player have their own armies, chosen from one or two factions. In many autobattlers, we see a consensus evolve over what players should be doing—and play tends to focus on a small number of orthodox strategies. If players have their own resources, however, then, they are learning how best to use what they have access to instead. They learn the strengths and vulnerabilities they face, and their experience and play is their own. Of course, we would like to see players have access to a variety of Squads, but each one should be fun and interesting in its own right.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/fae0613ec17f4da22598e44fd4cbbaac10c01185.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/78549ec408d1a9f495f547c5c70e64761d89aaf6.png[/img]
During the course of a game, we want to see a player’s Vanguard grow, and so we settled on a dead-simple approach. 

After each battle, players are offered two random creatures or actions from their Squad, as well as one of their “unlimited” free units. Players must take one of these three things, and since there is always a free unit available, they can always take that, even if they can’t afford anything else at the time. Players can lock in units or actions that they want to buy later. They gain only one gold piece each battle unless they get a room that generates gold or a creature that generates gold. 

This approach has taken a lot of tinkering and is probably not entirely settled as of yet. There have been iterations with too much gold, where players are just taking their most expensive units each time, as well as iterations with too much control of what can be purchased, so players settle on playing their Squad the same way every time. This method of growing your army is elegant and understandable to the first-time player—but it is vitally important that most games provide interesting choices for how to grow: whether to lock a unit or not, whether to save up gold or spend it. I think we are getting close, and we have the tools to get there, but once things are more fleshed out, a broader playtest group will help make it right. This is where feedback from you, the players, will really help. 


[b]Working with The Tea Division
[/b]
This partnership has been fun, though it has put me in the unusual position of needing to rein in my own designs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/8d70052fa200079f3f4c512b7a2cf0a7d07f5fa3.png[/img]

One of the things I love about working with The Tea Division is that they’ll work out how to implement any design I want to see. I am used to just doing everything with no limitations to see what works best and then working around the limitations of both the design and reality. 

The Tea Division has been so accommodating that I’ve found that I’m the one pushing, for example, for limits on how many units can go in a room. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/e1fb4f6eaa6ea97c4c27fa5557cdfdaefed6b8c4.jpg[/img]

I expected complaints about the interface and to work with those complaints. Instead, they made it open-ended, and I found myself playing games with dozens of units in a room. You will see, though, throughout the design are many elements you might expect to have a hard cap. Again, however, a lot of work has been put into making it open-ended. There is no specific hand size limit, and the map can get surprisingly large. 

Before I decided  the game would be better with a room deployment limit, you could freely deploy everything in a single corridor if you wanted. This open-endedness contrasts with many other games in which there are a precise number of slots for everything. What we’ve done has proven to be an exciting way to explore this game space, and we are enjoying developing it as much as I hope you, the players, are enjoying playing it.


[b]Analysis
[/b]
One of the things that has given me the most pleasure in developing this game has been the analysis tools we have been able to use. When we deploy and get destroyed, we can run the battle a hundred or even a thousand times and determine if we got unlucky or if maybe we lucked out doing as well as we did. This ability to run battles and see how they might have played out helps to learn what good strategy is and what sort of outcomes you might see. A good army with poor deployment can easily end up losing, and there is generally no perfect deployment—if your opponent knows where you are going, they will be able to take advantage of that.

I am not sure how best to give players access to analysis tools like these, but I have long advocated that players be included in some way. It is my experience that games with depth are more fun the better you are, and thus anything that helps players get better will make them enjoy the game more. Also, it is just fun to see. For example, a ridiculous string of things have to happen for a losing squad with a 1 percent chance of doing so to sweep the board. With that knowledge, one looks at future battles in a different way: with myriad different ways the battle might spiral out of control or be miraculously brought back from the brink of doom.

This is another thing The Tea Division has run with, and will be available in the next update of the demo. This will give you the information to go skirmish by skirmish, so you can judge for yourselves if your strategy was good but you got hit with bad luck, all the way to having a weak strategy and just being lucky!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/9e18cc8a993dc783fbd0f7ab1f7e3f61ce3bd65b.png[/img]

[i]—Richard Garfield, designer, September 2024
[/i][/quote]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45109952/0d520c77119fac6a0a6e02bf060137b425ff2d62.png[/img]
Richard is already working on more updates, and the devs are eager and ready to start showcasing some of the features and progress being developed for Early Access. The one definitive thread woven into the very fabric of the game is the focus that both The Tea Division and Richard have on making Vanguard Exiles a game that they can not only be proud of but that the players can feel they were a part of. The devs are very open to feedback, suggestions, and community involvement, and The Tea Division has remained committed to addressing and responding to issues, questions, or feedback that the community has; we always welcome and encourage players to reach out, so if there’s anything players want to ask, share, or have explained, the door to us is always open. 


Until the next update, keep smiling and keep on skirmishing!

notes.title: Update: Demo v0.1.739
notes.content:
Hey all! Thanks to the feedback and requested info received from our players, we've managed to push out an update addressing some of the more poignant issues the community brought to our attention.

[list]
[*] Fixed data parsing issues resulting in broken game flow 
[*] Fixed elves with 100% evade 
[*] Fixed Alien Locust spawn chance being forced to zero 
[*] Fixed issues with Buffed Units not evading at times 
[*] Fixed soft locks due to UI not responding and players not able to hit the Ready button 
[/list]
The team can't thank players enough for their valued contributions and are eager to continue working with the community to make Vanguard Exiles the best it can be.
